baseline.assessmentRule: Contract/schema tests are contract evidence; API tests count only when they exercise the real HTTP and persistence boundary; UI connection requires a browser flow making real application API calls; integration evidence must cover the whole acceptance scenario. Synthetic fixtures and test-only signature verifiers establish development behavior, not pilot verification or external trust-provider acceptance.
baseline.pilotEvidenceLimit: Existing dated verification artifacts explicitly say synthetic development/staging and actualPilotDeployed=false. The example configuration pack is not a selected project pack. No actual project role assignments, field work IDs, snapshots, or owner acceptance evidence were found.

scenarios.provenScope: The new real-HTTP test creates and fails an Inspection, confirms an Observation, creates Issue and Actions, uploads remedies, records a failed reinspection, restarts correction, passes a current-cycle reinspection, signs a Vietnamese FM-09 through explicitly test-only MockTrustedVerifier, releases that Inspection, and closes the Issue with current-cycle evidence. It rejects pre-pass close, initial-only/stale/mixed-cycle/action-only evidence, stale versions, and report creation before Issue close. It then exercises the separate Owner Report draft, issue, receipt, dispatch, verification and close, keeping report readiness open until that distinct lifecycle finishes. All Quality records and commands in this path use published HTTP endpoints. Separate connected browser acceptance now creates/fails the Inspection, confirms Observation, uploads drawing/PDF evidence, creates Issue/Action, verifies correction, creates/links/passes reinspection, renders final FM09 and requests both test-verifier signatures through the UI, releases Inspection, closes Issue and completes distinct Owner Report receipt/follow-up closure. The failed-reinspection/new-correction-cycle branch is established by HTTP acceptance, not asserted as a browser branch. Post-close UI hides unavailable close readiness while preserving Owner Report readiness.
gaps: The test uses seeded demo project context and original evidence, synthetic uploaded files, and MockTrustedVerifier. It does not validate a real signature provider, selected project policy, site performance, or pilot acceptance.

A foreign-scope Evidence selection at Issue close is not tested: the API rejects creation of that evidence at upload with SCOPE_MISMATCH under the demo role scope. Do not claim closure-level cross-scope rejection from this test.
The test exercises SQLite only; no dedicated PostgreSQL closed-loop Quality acceptance suite is identified.
scenarios.nextWork: Latest exact-head CI after Billing & plans recovery, production trusted signature provider/adopted forms and actual project pilot; preserve fixture/legal boundaries.

scenarios.provenScope: Real browser/API flow completes permit review/authorization/activation; creates and idempotently replays a Stop through HTTP; exercises browser acknowledgement, verified Action remedy linkage, resume request, supervisor verification and explicit lift; proves lift does not reactivate the Permit, then requires separate SUP permit-resume approval. It proves CON self-lift and contractor resume approval are denied, stale Stop version is rejected, and the permit retains the exact immutable Stop v1 reference after later Stop versions. The required Hold Point inspection release is attempted and rejected with ACCEPTANCE_SIGNED. All evidence uses synthetic development demo actors and records.
gaps: The actual hold-point inspection reaches passed but release_next_work is rejected with ACCEPTANCE_SIGNED because the required approved legal acceptance snapshot/signatures are not configured. Resume verification therefore uses a passed, unreleased synthetic Inspection; do not treat this as signed/released inspection proof.

The stop is created through HTTP because the inspected safety UI exposes no creation command. Remedy Action and inspections are also created/transitioned through published HTTP endpoints; the browser exercises Permit/Stop transitions and displays the connected state.

Existing issue #112 asked to align the F-03 ledger only to backend_api_implemented and exclude ui_connected based on the then-existing mocks. This new real browser flow strengthens UI evidence, but does not justify full AC-S-01 or pilot promotion; root must update the authoritative ledger only after assessing its specific status vocabulary and remaining acceptance boundaries.

The flow uses dev CON/SUP sessions and synthetic evidence; it is not a field pilot and includes no selected project pack, actual work permit, equipment registry, project role assignments, or Owner/site acceptance.

New actual UI Equipment/Permit scenario independently proves failed-current-equipment atomic rejection and passing reinspection activation using synthetic trusted upstream Equipment/certificates/plans. Full combined Stop/remedy/signed-release/resume UI scenario and actual equipment provisioning/site adoption remain unverified.
scenarios.nextWork: Add/identify an authorized project-level Equipment registry/trusted provisioning and real current safety-equipment inspection acceptance path; configure the adopted legal acceptance form and signer authority so an exact-version Hold Point inspection can be released; then extend the connected flow to use those records without demo readiness claims. Retain pilot_not_run until selected-project actors, assets, permit, evidence and site acceptance are supplied.

scenarios.provenScope: Recorded real source upload/import, approvals, progress, delay/recovery, Notice/EOT, Owner decisions, exact approved revision, idempotency/version rejection and effective baseline revision. Validation artifact records all browser/API/contract/PostgreSQL checks passing.
gaps: Validation is explicitly synthetic development/staging; no actual pilot project/actor acceptance.
scenarios.nextWork: Use as the current implementation-stage example; retain pilot_verified as unavailable until field scenario and evidence are supplied.

scenarios.provenScope: Real HTTP acceptance covers BOQ activation, quantity measurement verification, claim calculation/recommendation, exact Owner adjustment/approval decision references, and separate append-only payment records with correction/cancellation/additional payment, replay idempotency, authority and stale-version rejection. PostgreSQL acceptance subclasses the same HTTP flow in an isolated PostgreSQL 16 schema when configured. The connected browser spec creates an API-backed Payment Claim draft and verifies role capability changes; a second browser spec tests API endpoints/replay directly, not a complete UI-driven payment execution. Trusted upstream contract/profile/accepted references are fixtures.
gaps: The browser flow proves draft creation and capability presentation only; no browser-led path spans quantity verification through Owner decision and separately recorded payment.
Acceptance fixtures use demo project configuration and synthetic data; no actual project BOQ, measurements, authorized actors, banking/ERP records, or pilot acceptance is included.
The PostgreSQL suite is environment-gated by DOUL_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN; its presence or a passing unit run does not prove a deployed project or external payment.
scenarios.nextWork: Keep F-05 promotion bounded to backend_api_implemented for the proven backend scope. Add browser-driven progression through Owner decision and Payment Record when user-facing coverage is required; keep pilot_not_run until selected-project and actual payment evidence are supplied.

HTTP tests cover expired witness/equipment-certificate denials, preservation of original failed commissioning test and uploaded-evidence retest, Owner partial handover with a scoped reservation, and warranty remedy/reinspection/closure. The API tests bootstrap trusted profiles and upstream accepted records/configuration. They do not prove end-to-end generation/acceptance of those upstream project records or a selected-project configuration pack.

scenarios.nextWork: Keep the authoritative F-07 promotion limited to backend_api_implemented for the implemented/tested backend scope. Add connected browser API transitions and validate against an actual project configuration pack before considering UI-connected or pilot status.

crossCuttingGaps.finding: The application now has ko/vi/en display selection, translated shared/domain UI labels for selected modules, localized numeric/date formatting, locale-specific form-field catalogs, and document localization catalogs. HTTP tests render and retrieve FM-20 previews in ko/vi/en with frozen language/catalog/source data; catalog completeness is checked across declared form fields. Completion UI tests switch display language across ko/vi/en, but use injected mock records. Vietnamese remains the legal completion-document baseline. The interface language does not change document output language; output language is explicitly selected per document. Translation metadata marks Korean approved master and Vietnamese/English draft pending local review. Therefore previous statement that no locale infrastructure or language output existed is stale, but approved project-required multilingual report coverage is not established.
crossCuttingGaps.gap: Complete local review/approval of vi/en catalogs, bind selected project required/control languages and controlling-language policy, and validate each required issued report/form by explicit output language, exact source provenance, legal original/template/hash and approved language version. Preserve Vietnamese legal original where required; display-language switching alone is not proof of multilingual legal reports.

mustBeSuppliedForSelectedProject: Chosen project and validated Project Configuration Pack, including pack/config version and selected required acceptance scenarios.
Real SUP, CON and OWN accounts with active project RoleAssignments; DES and ADM accounts/assignments for role-boundary acceptance.
Core qualification/certificate records, holders, scopes and validity/expiry dates for the actual pilot period.
Approved project, package, location and discipline scope assignments for each role.
Owner P1–P4 report routing, recipient references, acknowledgment/follow-up owners and due-time rules.
Adopted DOUL forms and legal original-form identifiers, plus agreed report languages / controlling language.
Named backup/restore accountable owner, restore contact, outage escalation line and an agreed recovery exercise window.
For enabled media: approved provider/runtime, data export/transfer decision, retention/deletion period, cost owner/limit, and representative approved field media set.

For AC-S-01: authorized non-secret equipment register/asset IDs and tags, the approved project process for provisioning them, current inspection/certification state and validity, and qualified operator assignment; do not invent Asset CRUD authority.
For AC-S-01: adopted legal acceptance form and exact version/signature requirements for inspection release, plus active SUP/technical approver RoleAssignments and any required qualification scope.

For AC-S-01: actual work scope/permit references, method statement and risk/emergency-control revisions, permit validity window, accountable safety parties, and approved hazard/correction/reverification evidence references.
evidenceToCapture: Project/config version, build/commit, actor-role setup references with no secrets, and generated business object IDs/versions.
Executed commands and outcomes, rejection reasons, linked evidence IDs, screen/log/document snapshot references, defects/workarounds and owner acceptance decision.
pilotPrerequisites.securityRule: Use account and secret references only in this inventory; never include passwords, tokens, private keys, or real personal identifiers.
